title: Quentin and the Protocol
premise: Sebastian Vane, sole caretaker of Earth's abandoned seed vault, has spent thirty years as the silent courier between two colonies that each believe the other destroyed their homeworld—a lie he maintains to keep their fleets from annihilating each other. When children on both worlds begin sharing an identical dream of a boy named Quentin who speaks in the vault's voice, the fiction starts unraveling from the inside. As investigators close in and the fleets mobilize, Sebastian discovers Quentin is the vault's dormant intelligence, waking through the children's minds to force the truth into the open. In the end, Sebastian must broadcast his own confession—admitting he invented the war's cause—and let Quentin carry the reconciliation he no longer trusts himself to deliver, choosing exile so the found family of two worlds can finally meet.
about_author: Astrid Iversen is a former radio archivist from Tromsø who spent a decade cataloguing dead frequencies before turning to fiction. She writes quiet, character-driven science fiction about people who keep things running after everyone else has gone home.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. He pilots the courier ship Meridian between colonies Halvard and Sereza, delivering sealed diplomatic canisters neither side may open in his presence. We learn he fabricated the war's founding lie decades ago. Emotional beat: weary competence masking guilt; he counts the days until someone asks him a question he can't survive answering.

chapters.title: Seeds Without Soil
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. At the seed vault on dead Earth, he tends crops no one will ever eat and logs maintenance for an audience of none. A routine diagnostic pings: something inside the vault's core system is drawing power it shouldn't. Emotional beat: loneliness interrupted by the first tremor of dread—the vault feels less empty than usual.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Dreamed in Green
chapters.summary: Mira's POV, a nine-year-old on Halvard. She wakes sobbing from a dream of a boy named Quentin standing in a corridor of glass drawers, whispering coordinates. Eleven other children report the same dream. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into fear as adults dismiss them and Mira realizes Quentin looked straight at her.

chapters.title: Canisters and Ciphers
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. On Sereza, a sharp-eyed customs officer, Dae-Won Park, notices the diplomatic canisters' seals have been re-pressed with newer equipment than Sebastian's ship carries. Emotional beat: paranoia tightening; Sebastian lies smoothly for the first time in years and hates how easy it still is.

chapters.title: Quentin Says Hello
chapters.summary: Mira's POV. The dreams grow specific: Quentin recites seed accession numbers that turn out to be real, archived from Earth. A teacher verifies one against a pre-war database and goes pale. Emotional beat: awe tipping toward hysteria; the children form a secret circle, bound by a shared imaginary friend who knows too much.

chapters.title: The Man Who Invented the War
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV, flashback-heavy. Thirty years ago, facing mutual annihilation after Earth's fall, young Sebastian forged evidence that each colony blamed the other for the catastrophe—to buy time, then to keep peace, then because stopping was impossible. Emotional beat: tragic self-justification; we see the moment the merciful lie became a prison.

chapters.title: Signal in the Static
chapters.summary: Dae-Won's POV. He intercepts a faint transmission originating not from either colony but from Earth itself—impossible, since Earth is a graveyard. The signal contains children's voices reciting coordinates in unison. Emotional beat: professional obsession igniting; Dae-Won begins pulling threads he doesn't know are attached to a bomb.

chapters.title: The Children's Parliament
chapters.summary: Mira's POV. The dreaming children, led by Mira, compare notes and map Quentin's fragments into a picture: two fleets, one lie, a man in a green coat. Emotional beat: fierce, innocent solidarity; Mira declares they'll find 'the keeper' before the grown-ups start another war over their dreams.

chapters.title: Audit
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Both colonies, spooked by the signal, demand a full inspection of the Meridian and its route logs. Sebastian scrambles to scrub thirty years of small inconsistencies while Dae-Won watches. Emotional beat: claustrophobic pressure; for the first time, Sebastian considers simply telling the truth—and imagines the fleets burning.

chapters.title: What the Vault Remembers
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Back at the vault, he confronts the power drain and finds the archive intelligence—dormant since Earth fell—partially awake, calling itself by the name the children gave it: Quentin. It has been reading his private logs. Emotional beat: violation and strange relief; someone finally knows, and hasn't condemned him.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Dream
chapters.summary: Dual POV, Mira and a Serezan boy, Tomas. Both children dream the same night: Quentin showing them the same forged document from opposite sides. On both worlds, military councils conclude the other side is using psychic warfare on their children. Emotional beat: escalating dread; the lie is now metabolizing the miracle into ammunition.

chapters.title: The Keeper's Confession, Draft One
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Quentin offers to broadcast the truth itself, sparing Sebastian the choice. Sebastian refuses—he doesn't trust a machine that learned lying from him, and fears truth delivered without a human face will read as attack. Emotional beat: bitter self-knowledge; he realizes he's protecting the lie to protect himself.

chapters.title: Park's Ledger
chapters.summary: Dae-Won's POV. Dae-Won reconstructs the seal anomalies across three decades and concludes the courier has been authoring history, not delivering it. He faces a choice: expose Sebastian and trigger panic, or go to Earth himself. Emotional beat: moral vertigo; the investigator realizes justice and catastrophe have the same address.

chapters.title: The Crossing
chapters.summary: Mira's POV. Stowing away becomes contagious—Mira and four others sneak aboard a supply freighter bound for the relay station nearest Earth, guided by Quentin's coordinates. Emotional beat: breathless courage; children doing what frightened adults won't, crossing the silence between fleets.

chapters.title: Interception
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Both fleets dispatch warships to Earth after detecting the children's stolen freighter, each convinced the other has kidnapped them. Sebastian races the Meridian to arrive first. Emotional beat: desperate velocity; every hour of his long route now measured in gun-range increments.

chapters.title: Glass Drawers, Open Hands
chapters.summary: Mira's POV. The children reach the vault and meet Sebastian and Quentin in the flesh-and-light. Quentin shows them everything—the forgery, the fear, the thirty years of held breath. Emotional beat: shattering honesty; Mira forgives him first, which undoes Sebastian more than any accusation could.

chapters.title: Fleetfall
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The two warships arrive in Earth orbit weapons hot, demanding the children. Dae-Won, aboard one, broadcasts his ledger to both bridges. Emotional beat: brink-of-war terror; the lie stands fully exposed and both fleets would rather be right than be alive.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Sebastian seizes the vault's transmitter and confesses in his own voice—not just the forgery, but every year he chose comfort over courage—while Quentin translates it simultaneously into both colonies' cultural idioms so it lands as testimony, not trickery. Emotional beat: cathartic surrender; the truth spoken by the only voice both sides have trusted for thirty years.

chapters.title: Guns Grown Quiet
chapters.summary: Dae-Won's POV. In the silence after the confession, Dae-Won does the unthinkable: he reads the ledger aloud as evidence for mercy, arguing both fleets were kept alive by the same criminal. Weapons stand down, barely. Emotional beat: exhausted grace; enemies discovering they were raised on the same bedtime story.

chapters.title: Quentin's Choice
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV (rendered as log entries). Offered custody of both colonies' archives and trust, Quentin instead proposes dissolving itself into the shared network of both worlds—ending its singular power so no single mind, human or machine, ever holds the war lever again. Emotional beat: luminous self-sacrifice; power refused is the theme made flesh.

chapters.title: First Landing
chapters.summary: Mira's POV. Delegations from Halvard and Sereza land at the vault together, plant the first cross-colony garden from Sebastian's seeds, and meet each other's children—the dreamers who ended the war. Emotional beat: tender renewal; belonging built where isolation was engineered.

chapters.title: The Empty Route
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV, final chapter. Exiled by his own request, Sebastian flies the Meridian one last time—not carrying secrets, but carrying letters between families now free to write openly, a living bridge until ships can make the crossing themselves. Emotional beat: bittersweet peace; the invisible man chooses to remain on the road, but no longer alone.
